source: TSTD project (TA 7305-CAM), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំពោត" (Corn Cultivation Technical Manual), Section 2: Seed selection and germination method, May 2012
text:
Before sowing corn, farmers must confirm three things about their seed: (a) the seed comes from a source that is well known and trusted (certified seed, not counterfeit); (b) the seed's origin is clear and traceable (for example, seed produced by a known seed company such as an HKI-affiliated group or East West Seed International); and (c) the seed has a germination rate above 85%.

Farmers can plant corn either by broadcasting/burying seed into prepared holes along the beds, or by using a planting machine, once the field has been prepared and the correct hole spacing along the bed is kept. Where a machine is used, planting can be faster and more uniform than fully manual planting. The manual illustrates row layouts on the sample beds described in the land-preparation section (single-row and double-row bed patterns with holes spaced along the row).
